clue.text: Road that's fast and dry calls for no tricks

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's first fast motorway, written here as MI
sere is a literary word for dry or withered

explanation.surface: A motorist on a dry, fast road asks for no funny business.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is the motorway from London to Leeds; its 1 is read as the letter I. In solo whist a player calls this bid, undertaking to take no tricks.
explanation.definitionFit: In card games such as solo whist this bid is a contract to lose every trick.

clue.text: A branch of mathematics for artisans

explanation.surface: Mathematical study is offered as fit for craftsmen.
explanation.definitionFit: The study of forces and motion is a branch of applied mathematics, and skilled manual workers were once called by this name.

clue.text: Gushes about the opening of … Ibsen's Ghosts

indicators.note: about means the word for gushes goes around the other letter

parts.note: spirt is an old spelling of spurt, to gush

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone raves about the start of the Norwegian dramatist's play.
explanation.walkthrough: Ghosts looks like the Ibsen play's title but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Spirits are ghosts, the apparitions of the dead.

clue.text: Material can be consumed 'and made again…

definitions.note: a past participle; the answer is the adjective, able to be done again

parts.note: rep is a ribbed fabric
eatable means fit to be eaten

explanation.surface: Cloth that can be eaten and then remade.
explanation.walkthrough: REP is a ribbed fabric used for upholstery. The clue runs on with its dots into 5 Down.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that can be done or produced a second time is capable of being repeated.

clue.text: Given a simple meal — cutlery provided

parts.note: a spoon is an item of cutlery
fed means provided with food

explanation.surface: Someone is handed an easy dinner, with knives and forks laid on.
explanation.definitionFit: Being given things in an easy, predigested form is the figurative sense of a baby's feeding by spoon.

clue.text: … making them spare material

indicators.note: making signals that these letters are formed into something new

explanation.surface: The dots continue a story of making a spare piece of cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: PETERSHAM is a thick corded ribbon used for hat bands and waistbands.
explanation.definitionFit: Petersham is a stiff corded ribbon fabric, a kind of textile.

clue.text: Country Donne thought was an island

definitions.text: Country Donne thought was an island

parts.words: Country Donne thought was an island
parts.note: the poet's famous sermon line denies that any person is an island; read cheekily, dropping its opening letter leaves a Gulf nation he seems to call one

explanation.surface: A nation the poet John Donne supposed to be an island.
explanation.walkthrough: John Donne wrote 'No man is an island'; drop the N and you have a Gulf state that is not an island at all.
explanation.definitionFit: This sultanate on the Arabian peninsula is a nation, and it hides in the poet's line.

clue.text: Father, nimble but not robust

parts.note: Fr is the abbreviation for Father, a priest
agile means nimble

explanation.surface: A priest who is spry but delicate.
explanation.definitionFit: Something fragile is delicate and easily broken, lacking strength.

clue.text: Colleague has daughter over to stay

indicators.note: in a down clue, over puts one piece on top of the other

parts.note: an ally is a colleague or associate

explanation.surface: A colleague's daughter comes round to stay.
explanation.definitionFit: To dally is to linger or loiter, staying longer than needed.

clue.text: Meadow flower's inferior point has dropped off

annotationWithheld.why: Meadow flower's inferior point has dropped off: LEA (meadow) + F (FLOWER less LOWER, 'inferior') fits, but then 'point' is left with no job and no definition remains
annotationWithheld.clue: Meadow flower's inferior point has dropped off

clue.text: She accepted the fare, and cut the savoury

parts.note: to clip is to cut or trim
a pie is a savoury dish

explanation.surface: A woman took payment and then sliced the pie.
explanation.walkthrough: A CLIPPIE was a British bus conductress who took fares and clipped tickets; 'fare' suggests food beside 'savoury'.
explanation.definitionFit: A bus conductress collected passengers' payments, hence a woman who took the fare.

clue.text: Almost try to be useful — what a struggle

indicators.note: almost means the word is not quite complete, losing its final letter

parts.note: taken as written
to avail is to be of use or benefit

explanation.surface: Barely making an effort to help turns into hard labour.
explanation.definitionFit: Travail is painful or laborious effort, a hard toil.

clue.text: Novel form of Napoleon's empire

explanation.surface: A new style of empire is designed for the French emperor.
explanation.walkthrough: Napoleon is not the French emperor but the pig who rules the farm in Orwell's novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Orwell's fable is a novel, and the farm the animals seize becomes the domain the pig Napoleon rules.

clue.text: Historian, as it happens, changing the ending

indicators.note: changing the ending tells us to swap the final letter of the word for another

parts.note: live describes a broadcast going out as it happens

explanation.surface: A historian revises how events turned out as they unfolded.
explanation.definitionFit: Titus Livius was the Roman writer who chronicled Rome's past from its founding.

clue.text: Sort of bag pickpocket may move to claim

parts.note: a dip is slang for a pickpocket

indicators.note: may move signals that these letters can be shifted into a new order

explanation.surface: A thief might shift a bag to claim it.
explanation.definitionFit: A diplomatic bag carries embassy mail free from customs inspection.

clue.text: Coffee a waiter wouldn't get?

explanation.surface: A customer wonders which coffee a waiter would never be served.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading takes 'waiter' as someone who waits: a person who waits gets nothing immediately.
explanation.definitionFit: Powdered soluble coffee is called this, and something immediate is what someone made to wait never receives.

clue.text: However big, it'll only hold a small part of the harvest

definitions.text: However big, it'll only hold a small part of the harvest

parts.words: However big, it'll only hold a small part of the harvest
parts.note: a barn built to store the church's tenth share of farm produce holds only that portion

explanation.surface: A grain store, however large, never holds the whole crop.
explanation.walkthrough: A tithe was a tenth of produce paid to the church, stored in a barn of this kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Such barns stored the tenth of the crop owed to the church, only a fraction of the yield.

clue.text: Ireland in hardship shortly? She'll be better off one day

annotationWithheld.why: Ireland in hardship shortly? She'll be better off one day: IRE (Ireland) inside HE..SS fits, but no reading of 'hardship shortly' gives HESS, and no source was found
annotationWithheld.clue: Ireland in hardship shortly? She'll be better off one day

clue.text: One-piece suit

parts.note: not a garment: in bridge, a suit in which a hand holds just one card

explanation.surface: An all-in-one garment.
explanation.walkthrough: In card games a suit is hearts, spades and so on; a hand with only one card of a suit has this.
explanation.definitionFit: In bridge a lone card of a suit in a hand is called by this name.

clue.text: Clothing daughter has, though not pretty

annotationWithheld.why: Clothing daughter has, though not pretty: the scan agrees, but 'daughter has, though not pretty' builds no part of SINGLET (no D in it), and no source was found
annotationWithheld.clue: Clothing daughter has, though not pretty

clue.text: Indiscreet story heard from denizens of the deep

indicators.note: heard tells us the words are spoken so they sound like the entry

parts.note: naughty means indiscreet, and a lie is a story

explanation.surface: A scandalous tale overheard from creatures of the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: These spiral-shelled molluscs live in the ocean depths.

clue.text: Door-to door white-goods salesman?

parts.note: white goods are fridges and washers, but here the white goods are bottles of a dairy drink delivered to each doorstep

explanation.surface: A travelling salesman goes house to house selling fridges and washing machines.
explanation.walkthrough: White goods means large household appliances in Britain; the clue reads it literally as something white delivered to the door each morning.
explanation.definitionFit: This delivery man brought a white drink to doorsteps, so he sold white goods from door to door.

clue.text: He meant to mix this fuel

indicators.note: to mix signals that the preceding letters are blended together

explanation.surface: He intended to blend this combustible.
explanation.definitionFit: Methane is the main component of natural gas, burned for heat.

clue.text: Hacks at this street to dig it up

explanation.surface: Journalists attack a road to excavate it.
explanation.walkthrough: Grub Street was the London street of hack writers, so its name means hack journalism.
explanation.definitionFit: The London street of hack writers gave its name to them, and to grub is to dig something out of the ground.

clue.text: Love to stare 'round and show rage

indicators.note: round means the word for stare encloses the letter for love

parts.note: to gape is to stare open-mouthed
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: Love leads to staring and then to a show of fury.
explanation.definitionFit: To go wild with fury or excitement is an informal idiom about behaving like an excited primate.

clue.text: For example, iron rock

explanation.surface: Iron is offered as an instance of a rock.
explanation.definitionFit: Iron is a dense metal, and a loud aggressive style of rock music shares the name.

clue.text: As an example, give the word for action

definitions.text: As an example, give the word for action

parts.words: As an example, give the word for action
parts.note: give is one instance of a part of speech, and that part of speech is called the action word

explanation.surface: Someone is asked to supply an example word describing action.
explanation.walkthrough: 'give' looks like an instruction, but it is the example: give is a doing word.
explanation.definitionFit: Grammar calls the doing word in a sentence by this name, and give is one.

clue.text: Animal, we hear, has this covering

indicators.note: we hear tells us the word is spoken so it sounds like the entry

parts.note: a hare is an animal like a large rabbit

explanation.surface: An animal is said to have this coat.
explanation.definitionFit: Hair covers the skin of mammals as a coat or fur.

clue.text: He knew the opening words of an entertaining story

definitions.text: He knew the opening words of an entertaining story

parts.words: He knew the opening words of an entertaining story
parts.note: the opening words are not a story's first line but the password that opened the robbers' cave in the Arabian Nights tale

explanation.surface: Someone could recite how a good tale begins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Open sesame' were the words that opened the thieves' cave in the Arabian Nights.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Arabian Nights tale this woodcutter overheard the password that opened the forty thieves' cave.

clue.text: Recall touching essay

parts.note: re means concerning or touching on
a tract is a short essay or treatise

explanation.surface: Someone remembers a moving piece of writing.
explanation.definitionFit: To take back or withdraw a statement is to recall it.

clue.text: Colonist, perhaps German? It could be

indicators.note: could be signals that these letters might be rearranged into something else

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a settler might be German.
explanation.definitionFit: A colonist is one example of someone who leaves home to settle in another country.

clue.text: Check whether to broadcast or conceal

explanation.surface: Someone must decide whether to air something or hide it.
explanation.definitionFit: To vet people is to check them, to show a film on television is to broadcast it, and a partition hides things.
